clue.text: Turn up with barge and river's easy challenge

definitions.note: a pushover is something that offers no real resistance

indicators.note: the word up itself is turned round, so it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned round
to barge someone is to shove them

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that tackling a river with a barge is no great test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' looks like a phrase meaning appear, but it tells you to turn the word 'up' itself round.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushover is a task or opponent easily overcome, so an easy challenge describes it.

clue.text: Soup in cooking vessel long time

parts.note: a pot is the vessel you cook in
an age is a very long period

explanation.surface: Soup left simmering in the pot for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Potage is a thick soup, the word borrowed from French cookery.

clue.text: Pair in grass in 5

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 5-across, a season

indicators.note: the pair is placed inside the word for grass

parts.note: to grass is British slang for informing to police, as is to sing

explanation.surface: A couple lying together on the lawn during some time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass looks like the lawn but is the verb: in British slang, to grass or sing is to inform on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring is one of the four seasons of the year, between winter and summer.

clue.text: Broadcasting old melody after new

indicators.note: the melody comes after the letter for new in the answer

parts.note: an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A radio station playing an old tune once more after something new.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme on air is being transmitted live, which is the same as broadcasting.

clue.text: Letter from Stone in English collection

indicators.note: the stone abbreviation goes inside the word for a collection

parts.note: a pile is a heap or collection of things
ST is the abbreviation for the stone, a British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A letter retrieved from an English museum's stone collection.
explanation.walkthrough: The stone is the British unit of weight, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal letter, as with the New Testament epistles.

clue.text: Ocean's supported by salt perhaps

definitions.note: a verb: to salt is one way to season food

parts.note: an ocean is a sea, with its possessive kept
something resting on another thing is supported by it

explanation.surface: The sea is carried by salt water, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Salt looks like a noun linked to the ocean, but it is a verb: salting food is one example of flavouring it.
explanation.definitionFit: To season food is to flavour it, and adding salt is an example of that.

clue.text: Explain poor clue: answer in revised edit

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in means the single letter goes inside the reworked word
revised means altered, so these letters are rearranged too

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An editor's note: this clue is weak, so put the solution into the redrafted version and spell it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' CLUE gives ELUC; 'revised' EDIT gives IDTE, with A put 'in' to make IDATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To elucidate is to make something clear by explaining it.

clue.text: American term for term?

definitions.meaning: reads as a word that Americans use
the second term is the school or college term

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as asking for an Americanism generally; really 'term' is the academic period, called a semester in US colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: A semester is a half-year teaching period, the American word for a college term.

clue.text: Bottle good as weapon

parts.note: bottle is British slang for courage, as is nerve
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bottle turns out to be a good weapon in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for courage or nerve, not a glass container.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve gas is a chemical weapon that attacks the nervous system.

clue.text: Ground covering soft reptile

indicators.note: the ground word wraps round the soft letter, enclosing it

parts.note: terrain is a stretch of ground
P stands for piano, soft in music

explanation.surface: A soft-bodied reptile buried under a layer of earth.
explanation.walkthrough: P for soft comes from piano in musical notation.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, which is a reptile.

clue.text: Amount Stipe's band returned for 5

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 5-across, a season

parts.note: a sum is an amount

indicators.note: the band's name is sent back, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: Michael Stipe was the singer of the American rock band R.E.M.

explanation.surface: How much a rock band is paid to come back and play a festival season.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Stipe fronted R.E.M., the American rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: Summer is one of the four seasons of the year, the warmest one.

clue.text: Killer lurks in Windsor Castle

indicators.note: something lurking in the words is concealed within their letters

parts.note: the end of Windsor and the start of Castle together conceal the whale

explanation.surface: A murderer is hiding in the royal residence at Windsor.
explanation.walkthrough: Killer looks like a murderer but is the killer whale; Windsor Castle is a royal residence west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The orca is commonly called the killer whale, so killer is a shortened name for it.

clue.text: Dynamo in wacky art genre accepting Oscar

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the other letter goes inside
wacky means crazy, so these letters go haywire into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written
Oscar is the radio code word for the letter O

explanation.surface: A quirky art movement wins an Academy Award, and its leading figure is a powerhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: ART GENRE goes 'wacky', giving GENERATR, and 'accepting' O puts it inside. 'Dynamo' suggests an energetic person, but here it is the machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a machine that turns mechanical motion into electricity, an electrical generator.

clue.text: Children that might be taken in disagreement?

definitions.text: that might be taken in disagreement?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: to take ... with someone is to disagree

explanation.walkthrough: The second half sounds like children being taken away in a dispute, but it points to the idiom take issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring in legal language, and also a point of contention that people argue over.

clue.text: Primate stopped by Saint in church recess

indicators.note: the primate is plugged with the saint, which sits inside it

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monkey halted by a saint in an alcove of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular vaulted recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: In character I'm Frenchman offering fruit

indicators.note: these pieces are placed within the word for character

parts.note: a person is a character, as in a play
taken as written without the apostrophe
M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A Frenchman in costume hands out fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: M for a Frenchman comes from Monsieur.
explanation.definitionFit: The persimmon is an orange fruit from trees of the ebony genus.

clue.text: An unsatisfactory lawyer in Californian county?

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
a lame excuse is an unsatisfactory one
DA is a District Attorney, a US prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A poor attorney practising somewhere in California.
explanation.walkthrough: DA is the American District Attorney; the question mark warns the county is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Alameda is a county in California's Bay Area, containing Oakland.

clue.text: Large Scotsman carrying a box south for Europeans

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the large Scotsman holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: Ian is the usual crossword Scotsman, a common Scottish name
the box is slang for television, TV

explanation.surface: A big Scot lugs a box down south, for some people from the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large' and 'Scotsman' together make the holder, split around what is carried. 'box' is British slang for the television, and Ian is the stock crossword Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: Latvians are the people of Latvia, a Baltic state, so they are Europeans.

clue.text: All for end in feud in Maltese capital

indicators.note: all stands for end, replacing it within the feud word

parts.note: a vendetta is a long-running feud
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Everybody wants an end to the feud in Malta's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Valletta is the capital city of Malta, the Mediterranean island state.

clue.text: By which meatballs can be made from stale lamb?

definitions.text: By which meatballs can be made
definitions.meaning: looks like a cooking method for turning old meat into meatballs
the letters of stale lamb rearranged spell meatballs, a word game

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a recipe for old lamb, but meatballs is the letters of stale lamb rearranged, and the device that does that is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearranging the letters of one phrase to make another is exactly this wordplay device.

clue.text: Current where Royal Navy lost form

indicators.note: the Royal Navy letters are lost from the word, so they are dropped

parts.note: current means modern, of today

explanation.surface: An electric current somewhere the fleet lost its shape.
explanation.walkthrough: Current is the adjective for present-day, not a flow of water or electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a form or manner of doing something, as in a mode of transport.

clue.text: Reportedly virus was airborne

indicators.note: as reported out loud, the word sounds the same as the answer

parts.note: flu, influenza, is a virus

explanation.surface: The news says a virus spread through the air.
explanation.walkthrough: Airborne looks like the way a virus spreads, but here it means flying.
explanation.definitionFit: Flew is the past tense of fly, so something that flew was airborne.

clue.text: One of The Four 5s cured freak in dale, they say!

definitions.note: 5 is SEASON, so The Four Seasons, the 1960s American pop group

indicators.note: a freak that is cured is reformed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word for a dale is said out loud and the spoken sound gives the surname

parts.note: a dale is a valley

explanation.surface: A weird figure in the valley is healed, people claim.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5 refers to 5-across, so the group is The Four Seasons.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankie Valli was the falsetto lead singer of The Four Seasons.

clue.text: 5 with Milan football team?

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 5-across, a season

parts.note: Inter Milan is one of the city's two big football clubs

explanation.surface: Is this the season when the Milan side does well?
explanation.walkthrough: Inter is the Italian football club Internazionale of Milan.
explanation.definitionFit: Winter is one of the four seasons of the year, the coldest one.

clue.text: The French in conversation in alpine hut

indicators.note: the French article sits inside the conversation word

parts.note: a chat is a conversation
le is the masculine French word for the

explanation.surface: Speaking French while chatting inside a mountain cabin.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden cottage of the kind built in the Swiss Alps.

clue.text: See 21
Checking out will, hide what's altered

clue.text: Celebs magazine that man will love

parts.note: he'll is the contraction of he will
love is nil, which looks like the letter O, in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: He is going to love a celebrity magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Hello! is a British celebrity gossip magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello! is a weekly magazine of celebrity news and photo spreads.

clue.text: Gold corporation first to notice 5

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 5-across, a season

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
corporation is old slang for a pot belly, also called a tum

indicators.note: only the opening letter of notice is taken

parts.note: only its opening letter is used

explanation.surface: A gold company is the first to spot the season.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation is jocular old British slang for a large belly, here a tum.
explanation.definitionFit: Autumn is one of the four seasons, between summer and winter.

clue.text: Take and sell bananas wasted

indicators.note: going bananas is going crazy, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A greengrocer told to take bananas and sell them before they go off.
explanation.walkthrough: Bananas looks like fruit for sale but is slang for crazy.

clue.text: One getting in the way of graceful swimmer's lovers?
